messages.subject: Re: object 'POST' not found
messages.body_plain:
Congratulations patohora, you've found a bug! Expect a new release on the 1.1 branch in a few days. It's a tricky one and has to do with where your function is created. When you use the directive RSourceOnStartup, for the typical case all of your data and functions will be defined in the global environment. Thus as you have found out, all of the CGI variables, and even the rApache functions, are never found. However if you use RFileHanlder /path/to/file::function, then an anonymous environment is created that contain your data and code and the rapache environment which contains the CGI vars and functions are attached to it as the parent environment. Hence, rapache is found by lexical scoping rules. The bug is one I introduced a few versions ago. I was using some really nasty C level environment tricks to assign the rapache environment to the parent of each function invocation, but I decided against that since finding out it's not really *standard R practice*. The solution is to create a named rapache environment, stick it on the search path, then run the user's method for each request. Read below for a comment on your config. messages.subject: New release 1.1.13
messages.body_plain:
Thanks to a bug found the other day, I'm releasing rApache 1.1.13.

The major change is that all rApache R functions (setContentType, etc)
plus the CGI vars are placed in an environment named 'rapache'
directly onto the search path right before the base environment. Prior
to this rApache would insert the environment into the lexical scoping
chain of user code.

Please test.

Jeff

messages.subject: Re: libraries not loading
messages.body_plain:
It's more a permission issue than Ubuntu issue. If you don't have write permissions in .libPaths[1], then R will try installing into local (/home/<user>/) folder, as Jeroen explained. You can add yourself to the "staff" group which has write permissions to site-library folder:

# adduser <yourusername> staff

and you should add also www-user (or nouser) to the group if you want to install packages from webapp. Then it's up to you... think like admins do. Take it easy on the root priviledges... =)

You should check this one:
http://stackoverflow.com/questions/3487329/installing-r-packages-available-for-all-users

but please avoid my "neat" solution... "to make errors is human, but to really screw things up, you need root access".
